subject: Request: consolidated penetration artifacts + scope reconciliation for HorizonPay onboarding
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@horizonpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: PentestLab <reports@pentestlab.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pen-test evidence + scope clarifications (HorizonPay onboarding)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for working with HorizonPay on the onboarding checklist. Our security team ran a quick review of the items you uploaded and PentestLab flagged two questions before we can mark the pen-test requirement complete: 

1) We have the summary PDF but we need the full report (redacted is OK) and the raw findings export (CSV/JSON) so our risk engine can ingest them.
2) Please confirm the scope: which public-facing domains and internal services were in-scope for the test (IP ranges, hostnames, and whether internal services behind VPN were included).

Can you provide those artifacts or point us to where they are stored? We also need the remediation status for any critical/important findings (CVE mapping preferred).

Appreciate a reply today if possible — our onboarding timeline is tight.

Best,
Alice Turner
Senior Security Program Manager
HorizonPay

--
HorizonPay Security Team
security@horizonpay.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Can Security + Eng pull together:

- Canonical scope list (domains, IP ranges, internal services)

Marissa, can CS please own the external delivery and the short human-readable summary we send to HorizonPay?

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: pen-test evidence + scope clarifications (HorizonPay onboarding)

Thanks Vivek — I can take lead on assembling the artifacts. Quick notes and asks for Dylan:

- I have the executive summary (redwood_pen_test_2026_exec_summary.pdf) in the secure bucket at s3://redwood-security/horizonpay/pt-artifacts/2026-09-15/.
- I do NOT have the structured findings export; PentestLab told me they can generate a CSV but we need to confirm recipients.
- We need an authoritative scope list from Eng that includes any internal hosts that were tested via jump host or VPN. HorizonPay specifically asked for IP ranges and hostnames.

Dylan — can you:
1) Confirm the list of endpoints/hostnames in scope (including internal services) and paste them here or link a short inventory?
2) Export any relevant application logs or attack surface inventory that PentestLab referenced (they mentioned an auth microservice and api.redwood.com).
3) If remediation work is in flight, add PR/CL links and owner names to the vuln tracker export.

I'll coordinate with PentestLab to get the CSV once we confirm recipients and will assemble a redacted full report for HorizonPay. Target to have a deliverable package by tomorrow EOD.

Attachments: none in this message.

Monica Patel
Senior Information Security Manager
Redwood Inference

- Admin/VPN-accessible: admin.redwood.com (internal admin UI), auth-service.internal (behind VPN), telemetry-collector.internal

I will:
- Export the detailed findings we have locally to vuln_tracker_export_SEC-4821.csv and drop it in the secure S3 folder (same path as Monica's note).
- Add PR links for the two active remediation PRs (GH-4627, GH-4634) and the owners (Rohan Mehta, Neha Kapoor) in the tracker.

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@horizonpay.com>, security@horizonpay.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, PentestLab <reports@pentestlab.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen-test evidence + scope clarifications (HorizonPay onboarding)

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the redacted full report (redwood_pen_test_2026_exec_summary.pdf) and the structured findings export (vuln_tracker_export_SEC-4821.csv). Summary of scope and remediation status below: 

Scope (canonical):
- Public-facing: api.redwood.com (LB), *.redwoodusercontent.com
- Admin/internal (VPN-restricted): admin.redwood.com (internal UI), auth-service.internal, telemetry-collector.internal
- IP ranges tested: 34.82.0.0/16 (prod public), 10.10.48.0/22 (test/private overlay)
- Lateral access: PentestLab did perform limited lateral movement testing from the jump box to validate segmentation; no chain to production data stores was achieved.

Remediation status (critical/important highlights):
- FIND-2026-001 (Critical) - Auth bypass on auth-service.internal: mitigation PR GH-4627 (owner: Rohan Mehta). In review, hotfix applied to staging, deployment planned 2026-09-18.
- FIND-2026-007 (High) - Outdated dependency with known CVE: PR GH-4634 (owner: Neha Kapoor). Patch merged to main, rollout in progress.

Attachments (redacted): redwood_pen_test_2026_exec_summary.pdf (full redacted report), vuln_tracker_export_SEC-4821.csv (structured findings).

Delivery notes: PentestLab has provided the original raw export; we redacted internal IPs and internal-only log snippets per our disclosure policy. If HorizonPay requires less redaction for automated ingestion, we can coordinate a secure transfer process (SFTP or AWS STS temporary creds).

Please confirm receipt and let us know if you want the raw PentestLab JSON with minimal redaction — we can provide it under a short-term access agreement.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Information Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pen_test_2026_exec_summary.pdf (application/pdf), vuln_tracker_export_SEC-4821.csv (text/csv)
